the EC response (in terms of ICAM- 1 and VCAM -1 expression) to physiological atheroprone and athero- protective mechanical stimuli is not the same as the EC response to the corresponding idealized mechanical stimuli of the same average magnitude, and the level of VC AM-1 expression of the nicotine stimulated EC was more sensitive to the atheroprone mechanical stimuli than to the atheroprotective mechanical stimuli.
the EC response is different to physiological and idealized mechanical stimuli and the EC response to an athero-pronogenic mechanical stimulus is elevated by the presence of nicotine.

the endothelial cell response to physiological mechanical and chemical stimuli is more complicated and less predictable than the response to idealized stimuli.

ECs exposed to physiological atherosclerotic stimuli are likely to express a different biochemical profile than ECs exposed to the idealized stimuli that are commonly used in laboratory experiments.
